memoryText: The LORD is my rock and my fortress and my deliverer, my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Psalm 18:2 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This verse comes from a man who has lived in caves and on cliffs, and who knows what shelter is worth. David loads one sentence with seven images of God.

A rock is solid ground. When everything else is shifting, it holds. A fortress is a strong place that an enemy cannot enter. A deliverer pulls out of danger. A refuge is a place to hide, and a shield is a defense held up between you and an arrow. A horn of salvation is a symbol of strength and victory, like the horn of a wild ox. A stronghold is a high place that cannot be reached.

Each image answers a different fear. When you feel unstable, God is a rock. When you feel attacked, he is a fortress and a shield. When you are trapped, he is a deliverer. When you are exposed, he is a refuge. When you feel weak, he is a horn of salvation. When you feel overwhelmed, he is a stronghold. David does not say that God gives these things. He says that God is these things.

Notice the repeated “my.” David is not describing a general idea of divine power. He is speaking of the LORD as his own. It is personal faith.

Christians have always read this verse in the light of Christ. He is the rock (1 Corinthians 10:4), the cornerstone (1 Peter 2:6), the shield of faith’s defender (Ephesians 6:16), and the horn of salvation raised up for us (Luke 1:69). Each time you read this verse, you may fill in the name of Jesus.
weekInReview: This week you followed David as a fugitive. You read how the priests at Nob were slaughtered, how the distressed and the indebted gathered to David at Adullam, and how God guided him through the wilderness. You saw David spare Saul twice, and you saw Abigail turn aside his anger against Nabal. In the Psalms, you heard David’s love for the LORD in Psalm 18, his testimony of rescue and the God who equips with gentleness, and prayers in Psalms 54 and 59 from the hardest nights. The week taught that vengeance belongs to the LORD, that waiting is an act of faith, and that the God who delivers is both a rock and a gentle helper.
reflectionQuestions: David refused to seize the throne by force and waited on God’s timing. What is God asking you to wait for rather than grab?
David praised God as rock, fortress, and deliverer. Which of those images do you most need this week, and how does Jesus fulfill it?
Abigail’s wisdom turned David from a sin. Who has God used to correct you, and how might you thank them?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that he is your rock, fortress, and deliverer.
Thank him for the gentleness that makes you great.
